neighbours.label: assimilating to another group or person: becoming one of them, fitting in with them, living, speaking or dressing like them, following in their footsteps; peaks on the word that points at the group being joined ('them', 'of', 'with', 'footsteps')
fire: After ten years among the fishermen she talked, ate and even swore like them.
The orphan was taken in by the nomads and grew up as one of them.
To be accepted at the new office he started dressing and joking like his colleagues.
Her father was a surgeon, and she always meant to follow in his footsteps.
The traders settled in the port, married local women and became part of the community.
New students quickly change their slang so as to fit in with the older ones.
The captured sailor learned the islanders' tongue and was adopted into their tribe.
He so admired the monks that he shaved his head and began to live as they did.
quiet: After ten years among the fishermen she wrote a long book about the harbor.
The orphan was taken in by the nomads and given a warm blanket and some milk.
At the new office he started arriving early and leaving before the traffic.
Her father was a surgeon, and she always meant to send him a letter.
The traders stopped in the port, sold their cloth and sailed away in the spring.
New students quickly lose their timetables and have to ask for another copy.
The captured sailor counted the islanders' canoes and drew a map of the bay.
He so disliked the monks that he packed his bag and took the first bus home.

notes: Card: 'become members of their tribe', 'dressed like him', 'follow in his steps', 'fit in with'. Probes: 'became one of them' 0.58, 'spoke like them' 0.78, 'fit in with' 0.42, 'in his footsteps' 0.56; controls with the same people but no assimilation 0.04-0.24.
